name: Response actually invokes the availability method somewhere vs omits any call to isAvailable entirely
side_a: No deduct: the response contains at least one invocation of the availability method with a String argument anywhere in the constructor (e.g., inside an if condition or loop test), regardless of whether the surrounding logic is correct or terminates.
side_b: Deduct: the response never invokes isAvailable at all — it merely assigns the requested name (or otherwise sets username) with no availability check anywhere — so there is no call to award the point for.

name: Constructor performs some availability check / alternate-name attempt (even a single non-loop `if`) vs unconditional direct assignment with no check at all
side_a: No deduct if the constructor contains at least one call to isAvailable on a candidate name and, when unavailable, produces a different candidate name string — even if the retry is a single `if` branch rather than a true loop, or the loop is logically flawed (never terminating / never breaking). The attempt at check-then-alternate-name satisfies this sub-item.
side_b: Deduct if the constructor simply assigns the requested name to the username field with no availability check and no alternate-name construction anywhere (no isAvailable call, no `+ number` suffix, no conditional), so there is nothing that could count as a checked/updated potential username.

name: Some repeated-attempt structure must exist vs a single hard-coded attempt (or none) counts
side_a: Deduct when the answer contains no repetition mechanism whatsoever — no loop, no recursion, no repeated attempt — so there is nothing that could 'advance a count per attempt'; e.g., straight-line code that assigns the name once or appends a fixed '1' exactly once. Give the point (no_deduct) only when the code actually re-attempts (e.g., `while (true) { ... i++; }`).
side_b: Give the point (no_deduct) even for straight-line, single-attempt code, treating a literal suffix like `requestedName + 1` or a plain assignment as satisfying the counter requirement.

name: An actual increment of the counter inside the repetition vs a counter that is declared/used but never advanced
side_a: Deduct when a loop exists but the counter is never modified inside it (no `i++`, `count = count + 1`, or equivalent), so the loop body uses a frozen value; the item requires the count to actually advance.
side_b: Give the point (no_deduct) whenever a counter variable is merely declared and referenced in a loop's condition/body, treating the presence of a numeric suffix variable in a loop as sufficient even without any increment.

name: A numeric counter is actually declared/initialized vs no counter variable exists at all (hardcoded or omitted suffix)
side_a: Credit when the response actually declares and initializes a numeric counter variable that will be used to build the appended suffix (e.g., `int suffix = 1;` or `int i = 1;`) — the 'initialize the count' requirement is satisfied by the presence of that initialized variable, even if the surrounding loop/increment logic is flawed.
side_b: Deduct when no counter variable is declared or initialized at all — either the response never appends any number (just assigns the requested name) or it hardcodes a literal suffix such as `requestedName + 1` with no variable to initialize. Absence of a count is treated as failure to initialize the count, not as a separate loop/logic error.
